heads: Cyclone Akvan nears the Odisha–Andhra coast
Trump, Xi and Putin hold first trilateral talks
Delhi air back to ‘poor’; Bumrah strikes on return

paras.t: Namaskar, and welcome to Pringital News. Credible like print, fast like digital. This is your four-minute bulletin for Thursday, the nineteenth of November, twenty twenty-six, from New Delhi.

First, the headlines. Cyclone Akvan is closing in on the coast of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have held their first-ever three-way meeting. And Delhi's air has slipped back into the poor category.

Akvan is now a severe cyclonic storm. It is likely to cross the coast between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by Friday afternoon, with winds of ninety to one hundred kilometres an hour, gusting to one hundred and ten. About seventy-two thousand people have been moved to safety, and the Railways has rescheduled three trains.
Kolkata and Gangetic West Bengal are under a heavy-rain warning, with very heavy rain likely at isolated places on Friday. In Bangladesh, about a thousand tourists are stranded on St Martin's Island.

In Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, Xi Jinping hosted Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. Trump said the three largest nuclear powers should talk about cutting their weapons. Xi called for nuclear weapons to be banned and destroyed, and warned on Taiwan.

Delhi's air quality index rose to two hundred and eighty-nine on Thursday morning, after averaging two hundred and thirty-two on Wednesday. Pusa recorded three hundred and sixty-six. The city has fined more than twenty-five thousand vehicles this month and sealed over two thousand four hundred industrial units.
The Centre has told the Supreme Court that the probe into the June twenty twenty-five Air India crash in Ahmedabad is at its final stage. The court gave it two to three more weeks.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked industry at FICCI's centenary meeting to invest in the spirit of India First. He also met the Prince and Princess of Wales in New Delhi. Home Minister Amit Shah opened a two-day N.I.A. conference on cross-border terror.

The Sensex fell about five hundred points to eighty-two thousand and thirty-two after U.S. Federal Reserve minutes hinted at more rate rises. Auto stocks bucked the trend, with Maruti Suzuki up seven per cent. The rupee gained seven paise to ninety-three point four four to the dollar.

In Wellington, Jasprit Bumrah took three wickets on his return to Test cricket, and New Zealand were seventy for five. But Henry Nicholls made an unbeaten hundred and Glenn Phillips ninety-four not out, taking the hosts to two hundred and forty-three for five at stumps.

Ramayana collected twenty-three crore rupees on its fourteenth day, taking its India net total past eight hundred and forty-four crore. Ticket prices are being cut from Friday, when Dhanush's OM also opens.

At thirty-one, P.V. Sindhu is back in the world's top five for the first time since November twenty twenty-two, after a French Open final and a title in Germany. That's the news. Stay safe on the coast, and we will see you tomorrow.
